setup_summary.text: Fiscal Q3 (June quarter) was strong: revenue $109.42B (+16.4% y/y), diluted EPS $2.02 (+28.7%), operating margin 32.6% vs 30.0% a year earlier. iPhone grew 22% and Mac 29%, while Services slowed to 12% from 16% in fiscal Q2.

June-quarter quality of earnings: tariff refunds added about 2 points to company gross margin (50.1% reported, about 48.1% underlying) and $0.11 to EPS, so ex-refund EPS was about $1.91. Management said the underlying margin landed at the midpoint of its prior guide.

Management's September-quarter guide (given on the July call): revenue +9% to +11% y/y (about $111.7B-$113.7B on the $102.47B prior-year quarter), iPhone up mid-teens, gross margin 47%-48% including about 1 point of tariff-refund benefit, opex $19.1B-$19.4B. This assumes current tariff policy holds. It reflects a roughly 2.5-point sequential FX headwind and significantly greater supply constraints on iPhone, Mac and iPad.

Consensus sources disagree. Finnhub shows $2.02 EPS and $115.50B revenue (+12.7%), which is above the top of the 9%-11% guide. MarketBeat/FactSet show about $1.99 EPS and $113.3B-$113.5B revenue, which is within the upper half of the guide. The whisper EPS is $2.07. Both consensus sets are estimates, so we show both rather than pick one.

Our illustrative bridge from the guide (revenue and gross-margin ends paired, opex range, $350M OI&E, 16.5% tax, about 14.65B diluted shares, no mark-to-market) gives EPS of roughly $1.91 at the low end, $1.97 at the midpoint and $2.04 at the high end. A $1.99 consensus therefore needs a result in the upper half of guidance. The $2.02 (Finnhub) and $2.07 (whisper) figures need the top end or better. One point of gross margin is worth about $0.06 of EPS.

Supply and memory are the central issue. Management said supply constraints (advanced-node SoCs) will increase significantly sequentially in the September quarter. Memory costs rose in March and June and are expected to rise again in September, with market pricing still increasing beyond that and the carry-in inventory benefit shrinking. Apple raised prices on iPad and Mac, and management called elasticity too early to judge.

Positioning into the print: the stock is near record highs at $344.63, slightly above the $340.88 consensus price target. Loop Capital downgraded to Hold on Oct 20 (target cut to $330 from $370), and the options market implies a ±4.2% move vs a 2.5% average historical move. Apple has beaten in 3 of the last 4 quarters, with an average surprise of +1.7%.

This is the first report under CEO John Ternus. He and Tim Cook (now Executive Chair) took their new roles on Sept 1, 2026, and Cook said the June call was his last. December-quarter guidance and capital-spend and AI commentary will be read as the first signal of the new leadership.

Balance sheet and capital return are ample: nine-month free cash flow was $110.2B (vs $72.3B), cash and securities about $147B vs $84B of debt, and $25.8B of buybacks plus $4.0B of dividends in Q3. Authorization remaining is about $138B ($38.0B on the May 2025 program plus the new $100B), and a $10.0B ASR runs through fiscal Q4.

last_reported.text: Q3 FY26 net sales were $109.42B, +16.4% y/y.

consensus.text: Finnhub consensus is $115.50B (+12.7%). MarketBeat/FactSet is about $113.3B-$113.5B, about +10.7% on the $102.47B base by our arithmetic. IBD's quoted 7.6% growth does not reconcile with that base.

view.text: Anchor on the guide of $111.7B-$113.7B. FactSet-type consensus sits in the upper half, and the $115.5B figure is about $1.8B above the top of the range. Management said it will be 'scrambling' on supply, which argues against upside beyond the guide. The risk to expectations is a miss versus the higher consensus figure and, more importantly, the December guide.

last_reported.text: Q3 iPhone was $54.25B, +22%. Nine-month iPhone was $196.5B, +22%.

consensus.text: Yahoo cites iPhone consensus of about $56.58B, +15% y/y.

view.text: Guide is mid-teens reported growth. On the prior-year base of about $49.03B (FY25 $209.59B less nine months $160.56B), 15% is about $56.4B, so consensus is essentially at guide. Management said demand is high and supply-limited, with a 2.5-point sequential FX headwind to company growth. Watch for constrained units and ASP/mix after price increases.

last_reported.text: Q3 Services were $30.74B, +12% (vs +16% in fiscal Q2). Services gross margin was 75.6%, flat y/y.

consensus.text: Yahoo cites Services consensus of about $31.58B, about +9.8% on the $28.75B prior-year quarter (FY25 $109.16B less nine months $80.41B).

view.text: Guide is 'largely similar' to June's 12% after removing a roughly 2.5-point sequential FX headwind, which implies about 9.5%-10% reported. That is in line with consensus, and an analyst on the call read it as below 10%. Drivers: FX (about 5 points from March to September), no theatrical release vs F1 a year ago, softer App Store mobile gaming and the US link-out ruling. Offsets are advertising, cloud and payments records and 1.5B paid subscriptions.

last_reported.text: Q3 Mac was $10.35B, +29% on laptops, with MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro driving growth despite supply constraints.

consensus.text: Yahoo cites Mac consensus of about $9.69B, about +11% on the $8.73B prior-year quarter (FY25 $33.71B less nine months $24.98B).

view.text: Consensus embeds a sharp deceleration from +29% (supply constraints on Mac were the largest in June and will increase significantly; Mac prices were raised). Mac is the category where supply, not demand, most likely caps results, so the question is how much demand is deferred rather than lost.

last_reported.text: Q3 Greater China was $18.82B, +22% (nine months +30%), aided by a stronger renminbi, after a 4% decline in FY25.

view.text: The prior-year Q4 base is about $14.49B (FY25 $64.38B less nine months $49.88B) vs $15.37B for Q3 FY25, so the comparison is easier. No segment consensus was found. Watch for supply-limited iPhone and Mac in China and any commentary on the Siri AI rollout there, which still needs more regulatory work.

last_reported.text: Q3 total gross margin was 50.1% (about 48.1% ex tariff refunds). Products was 40.1% (refund benefit over 2.5 points) and Services 75.6%.

view.text: Guide is 47%-48% including about 1 point of refunds, so about 46.5% underlying at the midpoint, down 160 bps from 48.1%. The CFO said more than all of that decline is memory cost, with partial offsets from carry-in inventory, lower non-memory component costs and mix. Refunds shrink from about 2 points (roughly $2.2B) in Q3 to about 1 point (roughly $1.1B), so the refund benefit is a lower-quality swing factor. Each 100 bps is worth about $0.06 of EPS. HP's Personal Systems margin also fell on commodity costs despite price rises, which supports the memory-pressure read.

last_reported.text: Q3 opex was $19.08B (+23%), with R&D $11.73B (+32%) on AI infrastructure and headcount. SG&A was $7.35B (+10%).

view.text: Guide of $19.1B-$19.4B is flat to up 2% sequentially, or about +20% to +22% on the roughly $15.9B prior-year quarter. R&D is the swing item. AI compute spend also shows up in COGS, and management called the net effect of Siri AI on cost 'a bit uncertain'.

last_reported.text: Q3 effective tax rate was 17.9% (16.4% a year ago) and other income was $572M.

view.text: Guide is a tax rate of about 16.5% and OI&E of about $350M (excluding any minority-investment mark-to-market). That is a modest EPS tailwind from tax versus Q3 and a headwind from lower OI&E. Confirm whether the consensus EPS of $1.99-$2.02 uses these inputs.

last_reported.text: Q3 diluted shares were 14.715B, and $25.8B of stock was repurchased. Shares outstanding were 14.594B at July 17.

view.text: Our model assumes about 14.65B diluted shares (outstanding is already below the Q3 weighted average, with some dilution added back). A $10.0B ASR runs through the quarter and the final share delivery and price are set by VWAP. Share count is not a source of surprise unless buybacks slow.

last_reported.text: Components inventory was $7.65B at June 27 (vs $2.12B at Sept 2025). Other purchase obligations rose to $29.3B from $14.8B, and manufacturing purchase obligations were $57.0B.

view.text: Management attributes part of the gross-margin offset to carry-in memory inventory and said the benefit fades after September. A draw-down in components inventory, or a rise in commitments, indicates how much cost relief remains for December and beyond.

consensus.text: No current December-quarter consensus was found in the sources. On the July call an analyst said the Street was at roughly 8%-9% growth for December (stale). Commentary says investors will focus mainly on December guidance, Duo supply, China and gross margin.

view.text: The July call gave no guidance beyond September. Memory costs are expected to keep rising and the carry-in inventory benefit to shrink. Our read is that the December guide matters more than the September print, especially gross margin vs the roughly 46.5% underlying September midpoint and any lingering refund benefit.

since_filing.text: Leadership change took effect: the 8-K/A (filed Sept 1, 2026) confirms John Ternus as CEO and Tim Cook as Executive Chair effective Sept 1, 2026. Ternus's salary is $3M with a $55M target FY27 equity award, and Cook's is $2M with a $45M target award. This is newer than the 10-Q (July 31), which still lists Cook as CEO; rely on the 8-K/A. The Cook 10b5-1 plan disclosed in the 10-Q was scheduled to expire Oct 30, 2026.

Sell-side sentiment has cooled at the margin. Loop Capital cut Apple to Hold from Buy on Oct 20 and lowered its target to $330 from $370. Loop's supply-chain checks suggest Apple will not recoup about 13M iPhone shipments removed from its 2H 2026 plans, citing memory and processor shortages. MoffettNathanson stayed Neutral (Oct 20) and JP Morgan stayed Overweight (Oct 12).

Consensus has drifted down vs the earlier Finnhub figure: MarketBeat and FactSet show about $1.99 EPS and $113.3B-$113.5B revenue (Oct 26-31), against Finnhub's $2.02 and $115.50B. The two are the same tier, and the newer, dated figures are the MarketBeat/FactSet ones. The Finnhub figure is undated and above the guide's top end.

A 24/7 Wall St. article dated Oct 24 reports that Apple passed Nvidia as the world's most valuable company on "iPhone Duo Day" and refers to sold-out Duos. Another source (Oct 31) says the stock is trading near record highs. Investors are reported to be focused on December-quarter guidance, foldable iPhone Duo demand and supply timing, and memory cost pressures.

Peer read-across on memory costs: HP (10-Q for the July quarter) said memory and storage cost inflation and supply constraints will continue. Its Personal Systems ASPs rose 40.8% while PC units fell 15.8%, and its margin fell 0.8 points despite pricing, tariff refunds and FX. This is a proxy for the cost-versus-volume trade-off Apple faces.

Alphabet's September-quarter 10-Q (filed Oct 29) shows subscriptions, platforms and devices revenue up $1.4B y/y, with devices driven mainly by higher Pixel sales. This is a weak proxy for premium smartphone demand because Pixel is small.
Third-party India data (Counterpoint-based, Oct 24) put Apple at about 8% of Q3 shipments in a market down about 20%, with Samsung leading. This is a small-volume data point, not Apple-reported.

Source difference on supply: the call (before the July 31 10-Q) framed the binding constraint as advanced-node SoC capacity from stronger-than-forecast demand, and not a supplier problem. The 10-Q, which is newer, names advanced semiconductors, NAND and DRAM, and warns Apple may be unable to obtain components 'at all'. The two are consistent on rising memory costs, but the 10-Q is the more cautious.

key_debates.question: Can revenue land at or above the high end of guidance given supply constraints?

bull.text: Demand is running ahead of plan (iPhone +22% and Mac +29% in June), management called the constraint a demand-forecast issue, and FactSet-type consensus of about $113.4B is within the 9%-11% guide.

bear.text: Management expects supply constraints to rise significantly and described a quarter of 'scrambling'. The Finnhub consensus of $115.50B sits above the top of guidance, and Loop sees about 13M iPhone shipments removed from 2H plans.

key_debates.what_settles_it: September revenue versus the $111.7B-$113.7B guide, iPhone growth versus mid-teens, Mac and iPad commentary on constrained units, and how much of the shortfall is management saying shifts into December.

key_debates.question: How far does gross margin fall as memory costs rise, once tariff refunds fade?

bull.text: Carry-in inventory, lower non-memory component costs and favorable mix partly offset memory costs. Excluding tariff refunds, the June-quarter gross margin would have been at the midpoint of the guidance range given the prior quarter. Management says it reluctantly raised prices because of memory pricing.

bear.text: Memory cost increases are expected to continue beyond September while the carry-in benefit shrinks, and the September guide implies about 160 bps of underlying decline in one quarter. HP saw margin fall despite 40% ASP increases.

key_debates.what_settles_it: September gross margin versus 47%-48% (and ex-refund versus about 46.5%), the remaining tariff refund, and the December-quarter gross margin outlook.

key_debates.question: Will price increases and Duo-driven mix hold units and revenue, or does elasticity bite?

bull.text: Cook said pull-forward is 'not obvious in the data' given steady 22% iPhone growth, and the foldable iPhone Duo reportedly sold out at launch.

bear.text: Elasticity on iPad and Mac is untested, and HP's units fell 15.8% on a 40.8% ASP rise. Loop sees Apple not replacing the iPhone shipments removed from its 2H plans.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Unit and ASP commentary on iPhone, Mac and iPad, upgrader and new-customer metrics, and the December outlook.

key_debates.question: Is Services deceleration to about 10% a trough or a trend?

bull.text: Management attributes the slowdown mainly to FX, the absence of an F1 film release and mobile gaming. It set records in every category and has 1.5B paid subscriptions.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Services growth versus about 9.5%-10%, constant-currency commentary, App Store trends, and any update on the Supreme Court review of the contempt standard.

key_debates.question: Is the beat already priced in at record highs?

bull.text: Whisper EPS is $2.07, above the $2.02 consensus, and Apple has beaten in 3 of the last 4 quarters. The stock is trading in record-high territory ahead of the report.

bear.text: The stock ($344.63) trades above the $340.88 consensus target, Loop downgraded, and the options-implied ±4.2% move is wider than the 2.5% average historical move.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Reaction to the December guide (revenue growth and gross margin) rather than the September print alone.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Revenue at or above the top of the guide (about $113.7B+) and gross margin at or above 48% give EPS near or above the $2.07 whisper. The December guide shows easing supply and manageable memory costs, and the iPhone Duo and Siri AI add to the holiday narrative.

triggers: Revenue above $113.7B with iPhone growth above mid-teens
Gross margin at or above 48% including the 1-point refund
December guide implies growth near or above 9%-11%
Management indicates supply constraints peak in September

description.text: Revenue of about $112.5B-$113.5B and gross margin of 47%-48% give EPS of about $1.97-$2.02, in line with the $1.99 consensus. Services is up about 10%, Mac and iPad are supply-limited, and the December guide is cautious on gross margin as memory costs climb and the refund benefit fades.

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Supply constraints, FX and softer demand after price increases keep revenue at the low end (about $111.7B), and gross margin at or below 47% takes EPS toward $1.91. The December guide points to lower margins and slower growth as memory costs rise and the refund benefit disappears, which tests a stock above consensus targets.

triggers: Weak iPad and Mac after price increases
December gross margin guide below the roughly 46.5% underlying level
Commentary on lost iPhone shipments consistent with Loop's 13M estimate

claim.text: Component shortages and cost inflation (advanced semiconductors, NAND, DRAM): the 10-Q now says Apple is experiencing constraints and rising costs, expects them to intensify, and that price increases may not offset them and could reduce demand. The FY2025 10-K only described shortages as a past or possible risk.

Advanced-node SoC supply: management said the main constraint is advanced-node capacity with limited flexibility to remedy it. Cook did not commit to broadening silicon suppliers beyond noting Arizona-sourced components.
Price elasticity after price increases on Mac and iPad: Cook said it is too early to judge elasticity, and HP's units fell 15.8% as its ASPs rose 40.8%.

Tariffs and refunds: refunds from the February 2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling boosted Q3 margin by about 2 points and will add about 1 point in September, which is not repeatable. New Section 301 tariffs were recently imposed, and a Section 232 semiconductor action could follow.

AI compute capacity and cost: the new risk factor says Apple relies on its own data centers plus third-party cloud providers, that supply is constrained, and that it may over- or under-estimate needs. Siri AI's cost recovery plan is incomplete, and AI costs sit in both COGS and opex.

Regulatory limits on Siri AI and the App Store: DMA interoperability requirements have led Apple not to launch features such as Siri AI in certain jurisdictions. It is not launching on iPhone and iPad in the EU, and China needs more work. The EC can fine up to 10% of annual net sales in the Article 6(4) investigation.

US App Store commissions: the injunction bars commissions on link-out purchases. The Ninth Circuit said Apple can charge some commission on remand, and the Supreme Court granted review of the contempt standard on June 30, 2026. Apple is seeking a stay of district court proceedings.

Google search licensing and antitrust: Google's DOJ remedies are under appeal, and a reversal could prohibit commercial terms for search distribution. The DOJ's monopolization suit against Apple also continues.
CEO transition execution: John Ternus became CEO on Sept 1, 2026 with Cook as Executive Chair, and this report is the first under the new CEO.

questions_for_management.question: How much September-quarter revenue was lost to supply constraints by product (iPhone, Mac, iPad), and when do you expect constraints to ease?

why.text: Management guided to significantly greater constraints and said it will be 'scrambling', but gave no quantified impact. The size and timing of any carry-over decides whether December growth holds.

questions_for_management.question: What is the December-quarter gross margin outlook excluding tariff refunds, and how much refund benefit remains?

why.text: The September guide implies about 46.5% underlying margin, memory costs keep rising and the carry-in benefit fades; refunds are about 1 point in September with no visibility beyond.

questions_for_management.question: What are you doing on memory sourcing (long-term agreements, additional DRAM suppliers) and is pricing aimed at protecting gross profit dollars or percentage?

why.text: Cook called it a '100-year flood', said the DRAM market has three suppliers and that Apple is evaluating all options, with no formula for pricing.

questions_for_management.question: What are you seeing in unit demand and elasticity after the price increases, and do you expect to replace any iPhone production plan reductions?

why.text: Loop says about 13M iPhone shipments were removed from 2H 2026 plans and will not be replaced, while Cook said pull-forward was not obvious and elasticity on iPad and Mac was unknown.

questions_for_management.question: What did the iPhone Duo contribute in launch supply and demand, and what is its effect on mix, ASP and margin?

why.text: A 24/7 Wall St. article dated Oct 24 refers to sold-out iPhone Duos, and investors are reported to be focused on foldable iPhone Duo demand, supply timing and December-quarter guidance.

questions_for_management.question: Where is Services headed after about 10% growth in September: App Store gaming, link-out, FX, and the Supreme Court timeline?

why.text: Growth slowed from 16% to 12% on FX, no theatrical release, gaming softness and the US link-out ruling, and the guide implies roughly 9.5%-10% reported.

questions_for_management.question: What is the path and timing for Siri AI in the EU and China, and how will you recover compute cost (iCloud+ tiers, capex mix)?

why.text: Siri AI is not launching on EU iPhone and iPad, China needs more work, and Cook said there is no complete cost-recovery plan, with the capital-intensity effect uncertain.

questions_for_management.question: As new CEO, what are your priorities for capital allocation, buybacks (about $138B authorized) and AI infrastructure investment?

why.text: Ternus has taken over, R&D is up 32% on AI, capex was low through nine months and a large buyback authorization remains.

data_gaps: The Q3 earnings-release 8-K is not among the sources; June-quarter detail comes from the call and the 10-Q. The call is undated but precedes the 10-Q.

Consensus conflict not resolved: Finnhub (undated) shows EPS $2.02 and revenue $115.50B, while MarketBeat/FactSet (Oct 26-31) show about $1.99 and $113.3B-$113.5B. IBD's 7.6% implied growth does not reconcile with a $113.4B level on a $102.47B base (about +10.7%).
No December-quarter guidance or current December consensus is available; the only datapoint is a stale July analyst remark of 8%-9% Street growth.
Product-level consensus (iPhone, Services, Mac) comes from a single Yahoo video transcript; no iPad, Wearables, segment or Greater China consensus was found.

Reports of iPhone 18 Pro order cuts (Nikkei, Oct 9-11), IDC/Counterpoint/Omdia Q3 smartphone data (Oct 12-16; market down about 20%-22%, Apple share near 22%) and the Q2 memory price figure fall outside the 14-day citation window and were not used as evidence.

The iPhone Duo's price, unit sales and supply are not available in in-window sources beyond the 'sold out' report. A 2026-10-22 article on Apple production trims and Samsung price increases is secondary and unconfirmed.
Apple has not quantified the supply-constrained revenue, the remaining tariff refunds expected, or Services gross margin guidance.
The per-share impact of tariff refunds and the EPS bridge in this report are our estimates from guidance; Apple does not guide EPS.

A claim was removed because its sources don't support it: 'Management saw some headwinds in mobile gaming and said the App Store was a bit softer than expected, though it still set a June-quarter revenue record. The US link-out court ruling still applies, and Google search licensing remains exposed to the DOJ appeal. Consensus revenue of $113.4B implies growth of roughly 10-11% against $102.47B a year earlier.' (The CFO cites mobile gaming headwinds and a June-quarter App Store revenue record, but nowhere says the App Store was 'a bit softer than expected'; the rest of the claim (link-out ruling, Google DOJ appeal, 113.46B vs 102.47B is about 10.7%) is supported.).
